title: SPE Chapter 01 — Simple
_comment: VET THIS FILE before rendering. Each scene = one short narration beat (aim 5-10s) + one visual. lane 'app' shows the running page at app-relative path; lane 'code' shows the native GitHub blob with lines hl highlighted. Rebuild: RESYNTH=1 bash scripts/make-episode.sh 01-Simple

scenes.narr: This is a complete PHP web page: three pages, working navigation, and a real not-found response.
And the whole thing is produced by a single PHP statement, with no framework and no configuration behind it.
The entire program is this — echo, then a new anonymous class.
PHP builds the object and prints it, and printing an object is what triggers its toString method.
The pages live in one typed constant, each name mapped to a title and its HTML.
Because it's a constant, it's fixed when the file is parsed and shared across every request.
These two properties use asymmetric visibility, which arrived in PHP 8.4.
Anyone can read them, but only the class itself can set them — no getter boilerplate.
Here is the PHP 8.5 pipe operator handling the request.
Read it top to bottom: take the query parameter, trim it, lower-case it, and fall back to home when nothing is left.
So a messy input like this — spaced and upper-cased — still resolves cleanly to the About page.
Ask for a page that doesn't exist and the code returns a genuine 404, not a 200 that merely says not found.
That status line is what browsers, search crawlers, and the test suite all rely on.
Rendering is another pipe: the page names become links, and the current one is marked active.
The whole document is a heredoc — HTML written plainly as HTML, with no concatenation and no templating engine.
One habit from the very first chapter: the input is only ever used to look a page up, never printed back into the document.
So even a deliberate script-injection attempt simply becomes an unknown page and returns a clean 404.
That is the entire engine in fifty-seven lines. Next, chapter 2 gives the very same page a proper look — shared styling, dark mode, and an app shell.
